$schema_note: Source of truth for the generic Sage X3 SQL MCP. Each query has its SQL in sql/<name>.sql with /*FILTERS*/ markers; the filters below become [[ clause ]] optional blocks inserted at those markers. Run node build.mjs after any change.

settings.main_name: Query Sage X3 - generic agent and MCP server

groups.reference: Reference data: resolve a name into a code before any other query
groups.stock: Stock: levels by site, detail by lot and location, movements
groups.sales: Sales orders: ordered lines, the history
groups.revenue: Revenue: one aggregate to quantify, two details to explain
groups.purchasing: Purchasing and manufacturing: supplier references, component impact
groups.admin: Sage X3 dictionary: find the object behind a function or a screen

queries.name: x3_customer_search
queries.purpose: Find customers in the Sage X3 customer master (BPCUSTOMER) and resolve a customer name into its BPCNUM_0 code.
queries.returns: One row per customer: CUSTOMER_CODE, CUSTOMER_NAME, CATEGORY, CURRENCY, STATUS_CODE, STATUS_LABEL (Active / Inactive, local menu 1), CREDIT_LIMIT in the customer currency.
use_instead: x3_revenue_summary for anything about what a customer bought or was invoiced: this query holds no sales data.
queries.next_step: Use CUSTOMER_CODE as customer_code on the stock, order and revenue queries.

filters.name: customer_code
filters.description: One or more exact customer codes (BPCNUM_0), e.g. FR001 or FR001,FR002.

filters.name: name_contains
filters.description: Fragment of the customer name, case-insensitive partial match, e.g. urban.

filters.name: category
filters.description: One or more customer category codes (BCGCOD_0), e.g. FR or FR,PRO.

queries.name: x3_item_search
queries.purpose: Find items in the item master (ITMMASTER) and resolve a description into an ITMREF_0 reference. The default item entry point: short answer, 10 columns.
queries.returns: ITEM, DESCRIPTION (translated through ATEXTRA, falling back to ITMDES1_0), SEARCH_KEY, CATEGORY_CODE, CATEGORY_LABEL, ITEM_STATUS_CODE, ITEM_STATUS_LABEL, STOCK_UNIT, STOCK_TOTAL_ALL_SITES, STOCK_AVAILABLE_ALL_SITES. The stock columns are an all-site order of magnitude only.
use_instead: x3_item_detail for the full setup of an item already identified.
queries.next_step: Use ITEM as item on the stock, order and revenue queries.
queries.notes: Always pass at least one filter: the item master can hold tens of thousands of rows.

filters.name: item
filters.description: One or more exact item references (ITMREF_0), e.g. FIN008 or FIN008,FIN006. The most selective filter.

filters.name: description
filters.clause: AND (UPPER(ITM.ITMDES1_0) LIKE UPPER({{description}}) OR UPPER(ISNULL(DES1.LABEL, '')) LIKE UPPER({{description}}))
filters.description: Fragment of the description, case-insensitive, searched in the base language and in the translation, e.g. mountain.

filters.name: search_key
filters.description: Fragment of the item search key (SEAKEY_0).

filters.name: category
filters.description: One or more item category codes (TCLCOD_0), e.g. FINIS, SFINI, BMSOL, RAWMA.

filters.name: item_status
filters.description: One or more item statuses (ITMSTA_0, local menu 246), e.g. 1 for active.

filters.name: with_stock
filters.description: true to keep only items holding stock on at least one site.

queries.name: x3_customer_product
queries.purpose: Translate between the Sage X3 item reference and the customer's own item reference (ITMBPC), when a customer quotes a code that does not exist in the item master, or to list what a customer references.
queries.returns: One row per item x customer: CUSTOMER_CODE, CUSTOMER_NAME, CUSTOMER_CATEGORY, CUSTOMER_STATUS_LABEL, ITEM, X3_DESCRIPTION, CUSTOMER_REF, CUSTOMER_DESCRIPTION, ACTIVE_LABEL, ITEM_STATUS_LABEL, ITEM_CATEGORY_LABEL, the customer-specific units and packing (CUSTOMER_SALES_UNIT, SAL_STK_COEF, STOCK_UNIT, PACKING, PACKING_CAPACITY, PACK_UNIT_1/2, PACK_COEF_1/2, CUSTOMER_SHELF_LIFE_COEF), STOCK_AVAILABLE_ALL_SITES, CREATED_ON, UPDATED_ON, UPDATED_BY.
queries.notes: Many folders leave ENAFLG_0 at 0 (not filled in): filtering active=true then returns nothing.

filters.name: item
filters.description: One or more Sage X3 item references (ITMREF_0).

filters.name: customer_ref
filters.description: One or more of the customer's own item references (ITMREFBPC_0), exact.

filters.name: customer_ref_contains
filters.description: Fragment of the customer's item reference.

filters.name: customer_description
filters.description: Fragment of the description used by the customer (ITMDESBPC_0).

filters.name: description
filters.clause: AND (UPPER(ITM.ITMDES1_0) LIKE UPPER({{description}}) OR UPPER(ISNULL(DES1.LABEL, '')) LIKE UPPER({{description}}))
filters.description: Fragment of the Sage X3 item description.

filters.name: active
filters.description: Cross-reference active flag (ENAFLG_0): 2 yes, 1 no. Leave empty by default.

queries.name: x3_item_detail
queries.purpose: Read the full setup of one or a few identified items (ITMMASTER): management mode, stock, lot, serial, traceability, expiry, flags, statistical groups, units and coefficients, barcode, GTIN, customs code, buyer, planner, lead time.
queries.returns: About sixty columns per item; every coded field comes as a _CODE and a _LABEL pair, plus STOCK_TOTAL_A_ALL_SITES, STOCK_AVAILABLE_ALL_SITES, SITES_WITH_STOCK, CREATED_ON, UPDATED_ON, UPDATED_BY.
use_instead: x3_item_search to find a reference from a description: far lighter. Never browse a set of items with this query.

filters.name: item
filters.description: One or more exact item references (ITMREF_0). Prefer it.

filters.name: description
filters.clause: AND (UPPER(ITM.ITMDES1_0) LIKE UPPER({{description}}) OR UPPER(ISNULL(DES1.LABEL, '')) LIKE UPPER({{description}}))

queries.name: x3_stock_available
queries.purpose: Answer how much of an item is left, by site, from the ITMMVT totals. One row per item x site.
queries.returns: SITE, ITEM, DESCRIPTION, STOCK_UNIT, CATEGORY_LABEL, ITEM_STATUS_LABEL, STOCK_MANAGEMENT_LABEL, STOCK_ACCEPTED_A, STOCK_QUALITY_Q, STOCK_REJECTED_R, STOCK_TOTAL, ALLOCATED_DETAILED, ALLOCATED_GLOBAL, SHORTAGE_GLOBAL, EXPECTED_SALES_ORDERS, EXPECTED_REPLENISHMENT, IN_TRANSIT, PENDING_ISSUES, STOCK_AVAILABLE, REORDER_POINT, SAFETY_STOCK, STOCK_MAX, BELOW_REORDER_POINT, AVERAGE_COST, STOCK_VALUE_A, LAST_RECEIPT, LAST_ISSUE, LAST_COUNT.
use_instead: x3_stock_detail for lots, locations and quality control.
queries.notes: The figure to quote is STOCK_AVAILABLE (accepted stock minus detailed and global allocations), never STOCK_TOTAL.

filters.name: description
filters.clause: AND (UPPER(ITM.ITMDES1_0) LIKE UPPER({{description}}) OR UPPER(ISNULL(DES1.LABEL, '')) LIKE UPPER({{description}}))

filters.name: site
filters.description: One or more stock site codes, e.g. FR011.

filters.name: only_in_stock
filters.description: true to keep only rows with non-zero physical stock.

filters.name: below_reorder_point
filters.clause: AND {{below_reorder_point}} = 1 AND ISNULL(ITF.REOTSD_0, 0) > 0 AND (ISNULL(ITV.PHYSTO_0, 0) - ISNULL(ITV.PHYALL_0, 0) - ISNULL(ITV.GLOALL_0, 0)) < ITF.REOTSD_0
filters.description: true to keep only items whose available stock is below their reorder point.

queries.name: x3_stock_detail
queries.purpose: Answer where the stock is: by lot, sublot, serial number, location, warehouse, container, owner and status (STOCK table).
queries.returns: SITE, ITEM, DESCRIPTION, LOT, SUBLOT, SUPPLIER_LOT, SERIAL_NUMBER, LOCATION, LOCATION_TYPE, WAREHOUSE, CONTAINER, OWNER, STOCK_STATUS_CODE, STOCK_STATUS_LABEL (Accepted A / Quality control Q / Rejected R), STOCK_QTY, STOCK_UNIT, ACTIVE_QTY, PACKING_QTY, PACKING_UNIT, ALLOCATED_QTY, WIP_QTY, AVAILABLE_QTY, LAST_RECEIPT, LAST_ISSUE, LAST_COUNT, COUNT_IN_PROGRESS_LABEL.
use_instead: x3_stock_available for a simple total by site: far faster.

filters.name: description
filters.clause: AND (UPPER(ITM.ITMDES1_0) LIKE UPPER({{description}}) OR UPPER(ISNULL(DES1.LABEL, '')) LIKE UPPER({{description}}))

filters.name: stock_status
filters.description: Stock status: A accepted, Q quality control, R rejected.

filters.name: only_available
filters.description: true to keep only rows with a strictly positive available quantity.

queries.name: x3_stock_movements
queries.purpose: List stock movements line by line from the STOJOU journal: receipts, issues, transfers, adjustments, with signed quantities.
queries.returns: SITE, DOCUMENT_NUMBER, LINE_NUMBER, ITEM, DESCRIPTION, MOVEMENT_DATE, ACCOUNTING_DATE, CREATED_ON, MOVEMENT_TYPE_LABEL, DOCUMENT_TYPE_LABEL, SOURCE_DOCUMENT_TYPE_LABEL, SOURCE_DOCUMENT_NUMBER, MOVEMENT_FAMILY_LABEL, DIRECTION (Inbound / Outbound / Neutral), STOCK_QTY (signed), STOCK_UNIT, PACKING_QTY, PACKING_UNIT, ACTIVE_QTY, POTENCY, LOT, SUBLOT, LOCATION, WAREHOUSE, SERIAL_NUMBER, STOCK_STATUS_LABEL, VALUATION_PRICE, MOVEMENT_VALUE, COST_ORIGIN_LABEL, ADJUSTED_LABEL, BP_CODE, BP_NAME, USER_CODE, MOVEMENT_DESCRIPTION. Sorted by descending movement date.
use_instead: x3_stock_movements_summary as soon as the question is about a volume (how much went out in June): it aggregates on the database side.

filters.name: description
filters.clause: AND (UPPER(ITM.ITMDES1_0) LIKE UPPER({{description}}) OR UPPER(ISNULL(DES1.LABEL, '')) LIKE UPPER({{description}}))

filters.name: movement_type
filters.description: Numeric movement type codes (TRSTYP_0, local menu 704).

filters.name: document_type
filters.description: Numeric document type codes (VCRTYP_0, local menu 701).

filters.name: user_code
filters.description: User codes of the movement creator (CREUSR_0).

filters.name: stock_status
filters.description: Stock status: A, Q or R.

queries.name: x3_stock_movements_summary
queries.purpose: Total the stock movements by site, item and movement type over a period, on the database side.
queries.returns: SITE, ITEM, DESCRIPTION, MOVEMENT_TYPE_CODE, MOVEMENT_TYPE_LABEL, STOCK_UNIT, MOVEMENT_COUNT, INBOUND_QTY, OUTBOUND_QTY (negative), NET_QTY, TOTAL_VALUE, FIRST_MOVEMENT, LAST_MOVEMENT.
use_instead: x3_stock_movements only when the line-by-line detail is asked for.

filters.name: movement_type
filters.description: Numeric movement type codes (TRSTYP_0, local menu 704).

filters.name: document_type
filters.description: Numeric document type codes (VCRTYP_0, local menu 701).

filters.name: stock_status
filters.description: Stock status: A, Q or R.

queries.name: x3_sales_order_lines
queries.purpose: List sales order lines (SORDER + SORDERP + SORDERQ): which orders, which items, which ordered quantities. This is the history of what was ordered.
queries.returns: ORDER_NUMBER, ORDER_TYPE (raw code such as SON or WEB, no meaning to invent), CUSTOMER_CODE, CUSTOMER_NAME, SALES_SITE, ORDER_DATE, CURRENCY, STATUS_CODE, STATUS_LABEL (local menu 415), LINE_NUMBER, ITEM, DESCRIPTION, CUSTOMER_REF, ORDERED_QTY, NET_PRICE, LINE_AMOUNT_EXCL_TAX. Sorted by descending order date.
use_instead: x3_revenue_ordered for what is left to deliver (the order book).
x3_revenue_summary for a total or a ranking.

filters.name: order_type
filters.description: Order types (SOHTYP_0), e.g. SON or SON,WEB.

queries.name: x3_revenue_summary
queries.purpose: THE revenue entry point: totals aggregated on the database side and converted to euros, over both horizons, billed (SINVOICE) and ordered not yet invoiced (SORDERQ). Answers any total, ranking, trend or period comparison on its own.
queries.returns: LEVEL, REVENUE_TYPE (Billed / Ordered), YEAR, MONTH, CUSTOMER_CODE, CUSTOMER_NAME, ITEM, DESCRIPTION, DOCUMENT_COUNT, LINE_COUNT, LINES_WITHOUT_RATE, QUANTITY, REVENUE_EUR. Columns outside the requested level are NULL, that is expected.
use_instead: x3_revenue_billed or x3_revenue_ordered afterwards, only to explain a figure line by line.
queries.notes: LINES_WITHOUT_RATE counts the lines whose exchange rate to the euro could not be found: their amount is excluded from REVENUE_EUR and the total is then incomplete, say so. Billed and ordered are two horizons, never a cumulative figure. Credit memos and credit notes count negative, proformas zero. Always bound date_from and date_to.

filters.name: level
filters.description: Granularity, a single value: Total, Month (trend), Customer (customer ranking), Item (item ranking) or CustomerItem (what a customer buys item by item).

filters.name: revenue_type
filters.description: Horizon: Billed or Ordered. Both, comma separated, to compare them.

filters.name: site
filters.description: Site codes: sales site for billed, shipment site for ordered.

filters.name: currency
filters.description: Currencies of the source documents; amounts stay converted to euros.

filters.name: date_from
filters.description: Minimum date, included, YYYY-MM-DD: accounting date for billed, planned shipment date for ordered. Always fill it in.

filters.name: date_to
filters.description: Maximum date, included, YYYY-MM-DD. Always fill it in.

queries.name: x3_revenue_billed
queries.purpose: Explain billed revenue line by line (SINVOICED + SINVOICE): the actuals, with document type, shipment site, sales rep, statistical group, document-currency and euro amounts.
queries.returns: REVENUE_TYPE, DOCUMENT, LINE, REF_DATE (accounting date), YEAR, MONTH, CUSTOMER_CODE, CUSTOMER_NAME, SALES_REP, ITEM, DESCRIPTION, X3_CATEGORY, X3_CATEGORY_LABEL, STAT_GROUP1, SITE, SHIPMENT_SITE, QUANTITY, UNIT, CURRENCY, AMOUNT_CURRENCY, EUR_RATE, AMOUNT_EUR, STATUS_CODE (folder document type), STATUS_LABEL (Invoice 1, Credit memo 2, Debit note 3, Credit note 4, Proforma 5). Sorted by descending accounting date.
use_instead: x3_revenue_summary first for any total, ranking or trend.
queries.notes: Sign follows TABSIVTYP.INVTYP_0: credit memos and credit notes negative, proformas zero. An EUR_RATE of 0 means no exchange rate was found: the line cannot be converted, say so rather than counting it as zero. Always bound date_from and date_to.

filters.name: currency
filters.description: Document currencies, e.g. EUR or EUR,USD.

filters.name: invoice_type
filters.description: Normalised document type (TABSIVTYP.INVTYP_0): 1 invoice, 2 credit memo, 3 debit note, 4 credit note, 5 proforma.

queries.name: x3_revenue_ordered
queries.purpose: Explain the order book line by line: ordered and not yet invoiced (SORDERQ + SORDERP + SORDER). Quantity is ordered minus already invoiced.
queries.returns: Same columns as x3_revenue_billed with REF_DATE = planned shipment date and SITE = shipment site, plus STATUS_LABEL (line status, local menu 279), ORDER_STATUS_LABEL (415), ORDER_CATEGORY_LABEL (412), INVOICED_LABEL, ORDERED_QTY, DELIVERED_QTY, INVOICED_QTY, ALLOCATED_QTY, SHORTAGE_QTY, NET_PRICE.
use_instead: x3_revenue_summary first for any total or ranking.
x3_sales_order_lines for what was ordered historically rather than what is left.
queries.notes: Never add this revenue to billed revenue: two horizons, not a cumulative figure. Always bound date_from and date_to.

filters.name: only_open_lines
filters.description: true to keep only lines with a strictly positive quantity left to deliver.

filters.name: date_from
filters.description: Minimum planned shipment date, included, YYYY-MM-DD.

filters.name: date_to
filters.description: Maximum planned shipment date, included, YYYY-MM-DD.

queries.name: x3_supplier_item_code
queries.purpose: Translate between the Sage X3 item reference and a supplier's own reference (ITMBPS): the code to quote on a purchase order, reconcile a supplier acknowledgement or catalogue, list what a supplier references.
queries.returns: One row per item x supplier: SUPPLIER_CODE, SUPPLIER_NAME, ITEM, X3_DESCRIPTION, SUPPLIER_ITEM_REF, SUPPLIER_DESCRIPTION (often empty), PRIORITY, MINIMUM_PO_QTY (in purchase unit), PURCHASE_UNIT.
queries.notes: PRIORITY ranks the suppliers of one item: the lower the value, the higher the priority. 0 means not filled in, never top priority. Reference data only: it says nothing about what was ordered or received.

filters.name: supplier_code
filters.description: One or more exact supplier codes (BPSNUM_0), e.g. FR063.

filters.name: item
filters.description: One or more Sage X3 item references (ITMREF_0).

filters.name: supplier_item_ref
filters.description: The supplier's own item references (ITMREFBPS_0), exact.

filters.name: supplier_item_ref_contains
filters.description: Fragment of the supplier's item reference.

queries.name: x3_component_impact_chain
queries.purpose: Answer what breaks if this purchased component arrives late: the open work orders consuming it (MFGMAT + MFGHEAD), the finished item they produce (MFGITM) and the open sales order lines pulling that finished item. One row per component x work order x sales order line, the whole chain in one call.
queries.returns: COMPONENT, WORK_ORDER, WO_STATUS_LABEL, WO_SITE, COMPONENT_NEED_DATE, WO_START_DATE, WO_END_DATE, COMPONENT_QTY_STILL_NEEDED, COMPONENT_STOCK_SITE, COMPONENT_STOCK_AVAILABLE, FINISHED_ITEM, WO_PLANNED_QTY, WO_REMAINING_QTY, FINISHED_STOCK_SITE, FINISHED_STOCK_AVAILABLE, SALES_ORDER, SO_LINE_STATUS_LABEL, CUSTOMER_CODE, CUSTOMER_NAME, SO_CREATED_BY, SO_CREATED_BY_NAME, SO_CREATED_BY_EMAIL, SO_ORDERED_QTY, SO_DELIVERED_QTY, SO_QTY_TO_DELIVER, SO_REQUESTED_DELIVERY_DATE.
use_instead: x3_sales_order_lines only for the amount or the full detail of an order flagged at risk; the customer is already here.
queries.notes: COMPONENT_NEED_DATE is the date to compare a new expected receipt date against. COMPONENT_QTY_STILL_NEEDED is net of what is already consumed. WO_REMAINING_QTY = 0 with a non-zero component need is normal: the finished item is declared but the consumption is not yet recorded. Only firm and in-progress work orders (status 1, 2) are listed.

filters.name: site
filters.description: Production site codes. Strongly recommended: left empty, work orders of every site come back.

filters.name: finished_item
filters.description: Finished item references produced by the work orders.

filters.name: need_date_to
filters.description: Keep only work orders whose component need date is on or before this date, YYYY-MM-DD: typically the new expected receipt date.

queries.name: x3_payment_delay
queries.purpose: Measure payment behaviour on fully settled due dates: how fast customers pay us (receivables) and how fast we pay suppliers (payables), aggregated on the database side.
queries.returns: LEVEL, PARTNER_TYPE, YEAR, MONTH, SITE, PARTNER_CODE, PARTNER_NAME, DUE_COUNT, AVG_PAYMENT_DAYS (payment date minus invoice date), AVG_LATE_DAYS (payment date minus due date, positive = late, negative = early), MAX_LATE_DAYS, LATE_COUNT, LATE_PCT. Columns outside the requested level are NULL.
queries.notes: Only fully settled due dates are included (amount due minus paid = 0): the result describes past behaviour, not the open balance or aging. Year and month are those of the LAST payment date. Averages are per due date, not weighted by amount; below about 5 due dates a figure is not statistically reliable. A partner that is both customer and supplier appears under each partner_type. Always bound date_from and date_to (they apply to the payment date).

filters.name: level
filters.description: Granularity, a single value: Total, Site, Partner, Month, SitePartner, SiteMonth, PartnerMonth or SitePartnerMonth. Month means year and month of the payment date.

filters.name: partner_type
filters.description: Customer for receivables or Supplier for payables. One value per call: the two populations must never be added together.

filters.name: date_from
filters.description: Lower bound, included, on the PAYMENT date, YYYY-MM-DD.

filters.name: date_to
filters.description: Upper bound, included, on the PAYMENT date, YYYY-MM-DD.

filters.name: site
filters.description: Site codes of the due date (GACCDUDATE.FCY_0).

queries.name: x3_object_search
queries.purpose: Find the Sage X3 object code behind a business notion, a function or a screen: searches the object dictionary (AOBJET) by label, object code, function code or module, and returns the object's main table, primary key, main screen and management function. The first step before describing, listing, reading, creating or modifying an object.
queries.returns: One row per object: OBJECT_CODE (the 3-letter code used by every object tool), OBJECT_LABEL, MODULE_CODE, MODULE_LABEL, MAIN_TABLE, MAIN_TABLE_LABEL, PRIMARY_KEY (fields of the main index, e.g. SOHNUM), MAIN_SCREEN, MENU_CODE, FUNCTION_CODE (the GESxxx management function, when it exists), FUNCTION_LABEL, FUNCTIONS_ON_SAME_MENU.
queries.next_step: Pass OBJECT_CODE to x3_object_describe to get the screens and fields, then x3_record_list or x3_object_read.
queries.notes: Object codes are stable across folders (SOH sales orders, POH purchase orders, ITM items, BPC customers, BPS suppliers, SIH sales invoices, PIH purchase invoices, MFG work orders). A function code is usually GES + object code. Module numbers: 1 Supervisor, 2 Financials, 3 A/P-A/R accounting, 5 Sales, 6 Purchasing, 7 Stock, 8 Manufacturing, 9 Common data, 11 Sage X3 internal, 13 CRM, 14 Fixed assets.

filters.name: label_contains
filters.clause: AND (UPPER(ISNULL(TO_.TEXTE_0, '')) LIKE UPPER({{label_contains}}) OR UPPER(ISNULL(TF.TEXTE_0, '')) LIKE UPPER({{label_contains}}) OR UPPER(ISNULL(TT.TEXTE_0, '')) LIKE UPPER({{label_contains}}))
filters.description: Word of the object, function or table label in the folder language, e.g. order, supplier, invoice.

filters.name: object_code
filters.description: One or more exact object codes, e.g. SOH or SOH,POH.

filters.name: object_code_starts
filters.description: Prefix of the object code, e.g. SO to list SOH, SOQ, SOV.

filters.name: function_code
filters.description: One or more exact function codes, e.g. GESSOH.

filters.name: main_table
filters.description: One or more main table names, e.g. SORDER, ITMMASTER.

filters.name: module
filters.description: One or more module numbers, e.g. 5 for Sales.

filters.name: with_function_only
filters.clause: AND {{with_function_only}} = 1 AND F.CODINT_0 IS NOT NULL
filters.description: true to keep only objects that have a GESxxx management function, i.e. a real screen a user opens.
